lessons.title: Researching programs: the comparison worksheet
lessons.body:
## Start from directories, not from rankings

There is no meaningful ranking of PA programs. What exists instead is a set of published, required disclosures, and they are more useful than any list somebody sold advertising against.

Two sources build the initial list: the **ARC-PA** directory of accredited programs, which is the authority on accreditation status, and the **PAEA** program directory, which carries descriptive detail. Every accredited program is also required to publish its **PANCE first-time pass rate over five years**, its **attrition** figures, its **cost**, and its **program goals** somewhere publicly on its own website.

> **Key:** Everything below changes annually. Build the worksheet once, then re-verify every row in the spring of the year you actually apply. A prerequisite list you copied two years ago is a rumor.

## One row per program

| Field | Where it comes from |
|---|---|
| Program, city, public or private | Directory |
| Accreditation status and next review date | ARC-PA |
| PANCE five-year first-time pass rate | Required disclosure on the program site |
| Attrition for the most recent classes | Required disclosure |
| Class size | Program site |
| Total tuition and fees, in-state and out-of-state | Program site |
| Minimum cumulative, science and prerequisite GPA | Admissions page |
| Whether a last-60-credit GPA is calculated | Admissions page, or ask |
| Average GPA of the most recent entering class | Class profile page |
| Full prerequisite list with expiration windows | Admissions page |
| Whether online lab sciences are accepted | Ask in writing and keep the reply |
| PCE minimum, and average of the last class | Admissions page |
| Which PCE roles they count and how they weigh them | Admissions page, or ask |
| Test required: GRE, PA-CAT, CASPer, or none | Admissions page |
| Number of letters, and whether a PA letter is required | Admissions page |
| Shadowing: required or recommended, and hours | Admissions page |
| Supplemental application, its fee, and extra essays | Program site and CASPA |
| Deadline, and whether review is rolling | CASPA directory |
| Interview format and whether it is virtual | Admissions page |
| In-state or regional preference | Admissions page |
| Mission focus | Program goals statement |
| Seat deposit amount and date | Admissions page |
| Admissions contact, and the date you last verified | Your own notes |

## Three filter passes

**Pass one, hard filters.** A program is off the list if you cannot complete a required prerequisite in time, if your GPA is below a stated hard minimum, if it requires a test you will not take, or if its accreditation status is one you are unwilling to accept. This pass is arithmetic and it is ruthless, and doing it first saves months.

**Pass two, soft filters.** Cost, distance, how heavily they weigh patient care hours, whether they use a last-60-credit calculation, and class size. This is where an applicant with strong hours and an imperfect transcript sorts toward programs that reward that profile.

**Pass three, fit.** Mission, curriculum structure, rotation sites, and whether the interview format suits you. Fit matters least for getting in and most for the two years you spend there.

## How many, and in what proportions

Eight to fifteen programs is the usual working range. Against each program's **published class average**, sort your own numbers into three buckets: programs where you are above the average, programs where you match it, and programs where you are below. A list with nothing in the first bucket is a list that can produce zero interviews.

> **Trap:** Applicants routinely build a list of fifteen programs that all want the same thing, and then discover their one weakness disqualifies them fifteen times. Deliberately include programs that weigh hours heavily and programs that use last-60-credit GPA, because those are the ones whose scoring favors a career changer.

> **On shift:** Call an admissions office once with a specific question and record the name, the date and the answer in the worksheet. Admissions staff answer this kind of question all day, and a written note of who said what is worth more later than a remembered impression.
keyPoints: There is no meaningful ranking of PA programs; use the ARC-PA and PAEA directories plus each program's required public disclosures
Every accredited program must publish its five-year PANCE first-time pass rate, attrition, cost and program goals
Build one worksheet row per program with about 22 fields, and re-verify every row in the spring of your application year
Filter in three passes: hard filters that disqualify, soft filters that rank, then fit
Eight to fifteen programs, deliberately including some that weigh PCE heavily or use a last-60-credit GPA

checks.q: Which source is authoritative for a program's accreditation status?
choices: The program's own website
ARC-PA, the accrediting commission
A published ranking of PA schools
The CASPA program directory
checks.why: ARC-PA grants and withdraws accreditation, so its directory is the primary record and it changes between publication cycles elsewhere. Program websites and application directories can lag a status change.

checks.q: An applicant has 4,200 patient care hours and a 3.1 science GPA. Which filter decision best fits that profile?
choices: Apply only to the most selective programs, since hours will compensate
Apply to fifteen programs with identical weighting to maximize volume
Deliberately include programs that weigh PCE heavily and that calculate a last-60-credit GPA
Delay applying until the science GPA reaches 3.6
checks.why: Applying broadly to programs that all score the same way means one weakness disqualifies the applicant repeatedly. Programs weighting experience heavily, and those using a recent-credits GPA, score this specific profile more favorably.

checks.q: Why must the worksheet be re-verified in the spring of the application year?
choices: Because CASPA requires a signed verification form
Because prerequisites, deadlines, test requirements and accreditation status change annually
Because programs will not answer questions after April
Because GPA minimums are set by the state each year
checks.why: Programs revise prerequisite lists, drop or restore test requirements, and change deadlines between cycles, and accreditation status can shift. Applying against data gathered two years earlier is how a file gets rejected for a requirement that did not exist when it was researched.

lessons.title: Paying for it: cost of attendance, loans, forgiveness and service
lessons.body:
## Cost of attendance is not tuition

**Cost of attendance** is the school's published budget for one student for one academic period: tuition and fees, books and equipment, a living allowance, transportation, and loan fees. It matters for one concrete reason: it is the ceiling on how much federal aid you can borrow. All figures below are approximate and must be verified against current published numbers.

**Example one, a public in-state program over 27 months.** Tuition and fees around `$65,000`. Living allowance at roughly `$22,000` per year for `2.25` years, about `$50,000`. Total cost of attendance near `$115,000`.

**Example two, a private program over 27 months.** Tuition and fees around `$125,000`, the same living allowance of about `$50,000`, plus higher fees. Total near `$185,000`.

The difference between those two is about `$70,000` of principal, and after interest it is considerably more. Program choice is the single largest financial decision in this entire pathway.

## Undergraduate money is different from graduate money

**As an undergraduate**, the options include the **Pell Grant**, which is need-based and never repaid, **Direct Subsidized Loans**, where the government pays interest while you are enrolled, **Direct Unsubsidized Loans**, where interest accrues from disbursement, state grant programs, and employer tuition assistance. File the **FAFSA** as early as it opens each year, because some aid is awarded first come.

**As a graduate student**, subsidized loans do not exist. You borrow **Direct Unsubsidized** up to an annual limit commonly around `$20,500`, then **Grad PLUS** for the remainder up to the cost of attendance. Grad PLUS carries a credit check, a higher interest rate, and an origination fee of roughly `4%` deducted at disbursement, so borrowing `$50,000` delivers about `$48,000`. Federal rates reset every July `1`.

## PSLF, mechanically

**Public Service Loan Forgiveness** discharges the remaining federal balance after **`120` qualifying monthly payments**, which need not be consecutive. Four conditions have to be true at the same time for a payment to count:

1. The loan is a **Direct Loan**. Older FFEL and Perkins loans qualify only after consolidation into a Direct Consolidation Loan.
2. You are on a **qualifying repayment plan**, meaning an income-driven plan or the `10`-year standard plan.
3. You are employed **full time**, generally `30` hours a week or more, by a government entity or a `501(c)(3)` nonprofit. Most nonprofit hospitals qualify; many private practices and staffing companies do not.
4. The payment is made **while** all of the above hold.

Submit the employment certification form annually and whenever you change employers, so the count is verified as you go rather than reconstructed a decade later. The forgiven amount is not treated as federal taxable income. Terms have changed repeatedly, so confirm current rules before making a job decision on them.

> **Trap:** The employer, not the job title, determines PSLF eligibility. Two emergency medicine PAs doing identical work can have completely different forgiveness outcomes because one is employed by the nonprofit hospital and the other by a for-profit staffing group that contracts with it. Ask who signs the paycheck before you sign the offer.

## Scholarships and service obligations

Most scholarships are small, between `$1,000` and `$5,000`, offered by professional associations, program foundations, state organizations and employers, and a striking number go unclaimed because almost nobody applies. They are worth an afternoon each.

**NHSC Loan Repayment** offers up to roughly `$50,000` for a two-year full-time commitment at an approved shortage-area site, with larger awards at higher-need sites and part-time options at reduced amounts. It is applied for once you are working.

**The NHSC Scholarship** pays tuition, fees and a monthly stipend during school in exchange for two to four years of service afterward. It is competitive and it is applied for before or during training.

**Military pathways** include the health professions scholarship programs of the Army, Navy and Air Force, and the **Interservice Physician Assistant Program**, which trains serving members with full pay and benefits in exchange for a multi-year active duty obligation. Reserve and National Guard options exist with smaller obligations.

States run their own loan redemption programs for practitioners in underserved areas, New Jersey included, and terms change, so verify current eligibility directly.

> **Key:** A service obligation is a contract, not a discount. Breaking it triggers repayment of the award plus penalties and interest. Take one only if you would genuinely choose that setting anyway, in which case it is free money for a decision you had already made.
keyPoints: Cost of attendance includes living expenses and is the ceiling on federal borrowing; a public program can run near $115,000 and a private one near $185,000
Graduate students have no subsidized loans: Direct Unsubsidized to about $20,500 a year, then Grad PLUS with a credit check and a roughly 4 percent origination fee
PSLF needs 120 qualifying payments on Direct Loans, under a qualifying plan, while working full time for a government or 501(c)(3) employer
The employer determines PSLF eligibility, not the job, so a staffing company and the hospital it serves can produce opposite outcomes
NHSC and military programs are contracts with financial penalties for breach, so take them only for a setting you would choose anyway

checks.q: Why does borrowing $50,000 in Grad PLUS deliver less than $50,000?
choices: Because the school withholds a deposit
Because interest is prepaid for the first year
Because an origination fee of roughly 4 percent is deducted at disbursement
Because graduate loans are disbursed in quarterly installments
checks.why: Grad PLUS carries an origination fee taken off the top, so about $48,000 reaches the account while the full $50,000 accrues interest. That fee is one reason to exhaust Direct Unsubsidized borrowing first.

checks.q: Two PAs work side by side in the same emergency department. One is employed by the nonprofit hospital and one by a for-profit staffing company. What is the PSLF consequence?
choices: Only the hospital employee's payments count toward the 120
Both qualify, because the work site is a nonprofit hospital
Neither qualifies, because emergency medicine is not a public service specialty
Both qualify after consolidating their loans
checks.why: Eligibility follows the employer of record, not the location or the type of work. A for-profit staffing company is not a qualifying employer even when its staff work entirely inside a qualifying hospital.

checks.q: What is the main risk of accepting an NHSC scholarship?
choices: It reduces eligibility for federal loans
It is taxable income during school
It is a service contract, and breaking it triggers repayment with penalties and interest
It requires attendance at a specific list of programs
checks.why: Service obligation programs are contracts. The financial penalty for breach substantially exceeds the value received, which is why the decision rule is to accept only if you would choose that practice setting regardless of the money.

lessons.title: Prerequisites on the ground: regional options and the verification habit
lessons.body:
## Read this part first

Every institution below is named as an **example of a category**, not as a recommendation, and everything about it can change: course catalogs, which courses transfer, whether a lab is offered online, and whether a given PA program accepts it. **Verify current offerings with the institution and current acceptance with each PA program on your list, in writing, before you register for anything.** That habit is the actual content of this lesson.

## The categories, with regional examples

**Community college, for the cheapest credit.** In southern New Jersey this includes **Camden County College** and **Rowan College at Burlington County**. Community colleges typically carry the core prerequisite sciences, meaning anatomy and physiology with labs, microbiology with lab, general chemistry with labs, statistics, and general psychology. In-county tuition is commonly in the range of `$150` to `$200` per credit, which is the lowest cost per credit available anywhere in the path.

**Public four-year, for the degree itself.** Regional examples include **Rowan University**, **Rutgers University-Camden**, and **Stockton University**. These are where a bachelor's is completed, commonly in health sciences or biology, at roughly `$400` to `$600` per credit in state. Many now run evening, weekend and hybrid sections aimed at working adults.

**Adult-focused and online completion.** **Thomas Edison State University** is a New Jersey public institution built specifically for adult learners, offering credit for prior learning, credit by examination, and online degree completion. Nationally, competency-based online universities of the kind **Western Governors University** popularized offer flat-rate terms and self-paced progress at regionally accredited institutions.

> **Trap:** The sticking point for every online route is the same one: **lab science**. Some PA programs accept online laboratory courses and some refuse them, a split that widened after 2020 and has not settled. This is the single question to ask every program on your list before enrolling in an online lab science, and the answer should be saved in writing.

## Transfer, in New Jersey specifically

New Jersey operates a statewide transfer framework under which a completed associate degree from a New Jersey community college generally transfers to a New Jersey public four-year institution with junior standing, and a statewide course-equivalency tool exists to check individual courses. General frameworks do not bind individual majors, so confirm the specific degree program you intend to finish.

Two separate decisions are frequently confused:

1. **Does the credit transfer toward the degree?** That is decided by the four-year college.
2. **Does the course satisfy a PA program prerequisite?** That is decided by each PA program, and many will not accept science courses older than `5` to `7` years.

A course can pass the first test permanently and fail the second, which is how someone discovers that an anatomy course from `2014` counts toward graduation and still has to be retaken.

## Sequencing rules that hold regardless of school

- **Anatomy and Physiology I first.** It anchors the sequence, it is a prerequisite for A and P II, and it appears on essentially every PA program's list.
- **General Chemistry I before organic chemistry or biochemistry**, which are the courses most likely to appear as an uncommon requirement late.
- **Statistics and psychology are pairing courses.** They are the safe second course to take alongside a lab science.
- **Never two lab sciences in one semester while working full time.** A lab science is effectively two courses of work, and a failed prerequisite costs the retake, the semester, and the GPA.
- **Take science courses where you intend the grade to live**, remembering that CASPA pools grades from every institution regardless.

## The verification habit

For every course you plan or complete, record six things: the institution, the course code and title, the credits, the term, the grade, and which PA programs on your list have confirmed they accept it. Re-check the last column in the spring of your application year.

> **Key:** Two institutions make two independent decisions about every course you take, and neither one tells the other. The verification habit exists because the gap between those two decisions is where a whole cycle gets lost.
keyPoints: Offerings, transferability and prerequisite acceptance change every year and must be verified with both the college and each PA program, in writing
Community colleges such as Camden County College and Rowan College at Burlington County carry the core sciences at roughly $150 to $200 per credit in-county

Public four-years such as Rowan, Rutgers-Camden and Stockton complete the degree at roughly $400 to $600 per credit in state; Thomas Edison State and competency-based online schools serve adult completion
Online lab science acceptance is split among PA programs and is the single question to ask before enrolling in one
Transfer toward a degree and acceptance as a PA prerequisite are two separate decisions, and science prerequisites commonly expire at 5 to 7 years

checks.q: A course from 2014 transfers toward a bachelor's degree at a four-year university. What does that tell you about PA prerequisites?
choices: It satisfies the prerequisite automatically, since the credit transferred
Nothing, because the PA program makes a separate decision and many cap science prerequisites at 5 to 7 years
It only counts if the grade was a B or better
It must be re-evaluated by the state transfer system
checks.why: Degree credit and prerequisite acceptance are decided by two different institutions under different rules. A course can count toward graduation permanently while being too old for a PA program's prerequisite window.

checks.q: Which question should be asked in writing before enrolling in an online lab science?
choices: Whether the college is nationally accredited
Whether the course has a proctored final exam
Whether each PA program on your list accepts online laboratory courses
Whether the lab kit is shipped at no cost
checks.why: PA programs are split on online labs and the split has not settled. Since the answer varies by program and can change, it is asked of each target program and the reply is saved, rather than assumed from the college's own claims.

checks.q: Why is taking two lab sciences in one semester while working full time discouraged?
choices: Because most colleges prohibit it
Because CASPA penalizes overlapping science coursework
Because financial aid will not cover two labs
Because a lab science is effectively two courses of work, and a failed prerequisite costs the retake, the semester and the GPA
checks.why: The workload of a lab course is roughly double its credit count, and CASPA counts a failure permanently since grade replacement does not exist. The lost time is usually a full semester, not a few weeks.

lessons.title: Hours that survive verification
lessons.body:
## What CASPA asks for, field by field

Each experience entry requires: the **experience type**, the **organization name**, the **supervisor's name, title, phone number and email**, the **start and end dates** or an indication that it is ongoing, the **total hours completed to date**, **anticipated additional hours with a completion date** if it is ongoing, the **job title**, whether the position was **paid**, and a short **description of duties** with a character limit.

The experience types are patient care, healthcare, volunteer, employment, research, teaching, leadership, and extracurricular activities. You assign the category yourself, and the description you write is what a reviewer reads to decide whether the category is honest.

## Logging so the number is defensible

- **Log weekly, from the timekeeping record**, not from memory. A reconstruction built in April of the application year produces numbers you cannot defend under a question.
- **Record hours actually worked.** Overtime counts. Unpaid meal breaks do not. Cancelled and low-census shifts do not. Orientation and required in-house training generally do.
- **Keep one simple sheet:** date, shift start, shift end, hours, role, and a note on anything unusual. That is five columns and about ninety seconds a week.
- **Export the payroll time record once a year** and store it somewhere that survives leaving the job. It is the source document behind every number you will claim.
- **Capture supervisor contact information before they leave**, including an email that is not the hospital address if they will give one. Turnover in an emergency department is high, and a verifier who cannot be reached makes an entry look thin.
- **Ask human resources who the verifier of record is** if your supervisor leaves, and whether the employer uses a third-party employment verification service. Note the answer in the log.

## Projected hours

Hours not yet worked may be entered as **anticipated**, with a stated completion date, and programs expect this because the entire point is applying while still working. Two rules keep it honest: do not project past the date you realistically stop working, and be prepared for a program to ask you to confirm the final total later.

## Categorizing without cheating

Emergency department technician is unambiguously patient care experience. Scribe is healthcare experience. The dividing question is responsibility, not proximity: did the patient's care depend on something you personally did?

A genuinely mixed role is entered as **two entries with an honest hour split**, each with its own description, rather than as one entry claimed at the more favorable category. A reviewer who reads a description that does not match the category has found a credibility problem, and credibility problems are not survivable in the way a mediocre GPA is.

## Writing the description

Duties, in verbs, at the level of specificity a clinician would recognize.

"Obtain and interpret-ready `12`-lead ECGs, perform venipuncture and point-of-care testing, place and monitor cardiac telemetry, assist with procedures including splinting, wound care and orthopedic reduction, perform CPR and participate in trauma and code response, obtain and trend vital signs and report changes to the nursing and provider team."

That paragraph does more for an application than the job title ever will, and it also becomes the raw material for the personal statement and the interview.

## What gets a file flagged

| Problem | What a reviewer sees |
|---|---|
| Total that does not fit the dates | `4,000` hours claimed across `12` months is about `77` hours a week |
| Two employers overlapping implausibly | Combined hours exceeding what a human can work |
| A supervisor who cannot be reached | An entry that cannot be verified at all |
| A description that contradicts the category | Patient care claimed for duties that are clerical |
| Round numbers everywhere | `2,000` and `1,500` and `500` suggest estimation rather than records |

> **Key:** The arithmetic check programs run is simple: `36` hours a week for `48` weeks is about `1,728` hours a year. Any claim that cannot be reconciled with dates and a plausible schedule invites a question you do not want to answer from memory.

> **On shift:** The hours accumulate whether or not you record them. The record is the only part that does not happen automatically, and it is the part the application is built from.
keyPoints: Each CASPA experience entry needs organization, supervisor name and contact, dates, hours, title, paid status, and a duty description
Log weekly from the timekeeping record and export payroll time records annually; count hours worked, not scheduled
Capture supervisor contact details before turnover, and note the employer's verification service if one exists
Anticipated hours are allowed with a stated completion date, but never projected past when you would actually stop working
Programs check arithmetic: 36 hours a week for 48 weeks is about 1,728 hours a year, and totals that cannot be reconciled invite questions

checks.q: An applicant claims 4,000 patient care hours accumulated over 12 months. What will a reviewer notice?
choices: Nothing, since hours have no annual ceiling
That this averages about 77 hours a week, which does not reconcile with a single full-time job
That the total is below the competitive average
That anticipated hours were not declared
checks.why: Programs do the division. About 1,728 hours a year is a full-time clinical schedule, so 4,000 in a single year requires either two jobs documented separately or an error, and either way it prompts a question.

checks.q: A role involves both hands-on patient care and clerical unit duties. How should it be entered?
choices: As one patient care entry, since the patient care portion is the more meaningful part
As two entries with an honest hour split and separate descriptions
As one healthcare experience entry to stay safe
As a volunteer entry, since the categories do not fit
checks.why: Splitting the role keeps each description matched to its category, which is what a reviewer actually checks. Claiming the whole thing as patient care creates a mismatch between the duties described and the category chosen, which reads as a credibility problem.

checks.q: Why capture a supervisor's contact information early rather than at application time?
choices: Because CASPA requires contact details to be more than a year old
Because supervisors must approve hours monthly
Because turnover is high and an unreachable verifier makes an otherwise strong entry unverifiable
Because programs contact supervisors before interviews are offered
checks.why: Emergency department staffing turns over, and an entry whose verifier has left with no forwarding contact cannot be confirmed. Capturing the information while the relationship is current costs nothing and protects thousands of hours.

lessons.title: CASPA, section by section
lessons.body:
## The six sections

**1. Personal Information.** Biographic details, contact information, citizenship, and a set of background questions covering academic and legal history. Use the **legal name that appears on your transcripts**, or verification stalls while records are matched.

> **Trap:** Answer the background questions honestly and briefly. A disclosed issue with a two-sentence factual explanation is routinely survivable. The same issue discovered later, after nondisclosure, is an integrity finding and it ends applications and sometimes enrollments.

**2. Academic History.** Three parts, and this section is where cycles are lost.

- **Colleges Attended:** every institution you ever enrolled in, including the one semester twenty years ago and the summer class at a school you never returned to. Omission is an integrity problem, and CASPA finds them.
- **Transcripts:** requested as official documents sent directly from each institution, usually with a CASPA-generated request form attached so they are matched to your file.
- **Coursework:** every course entered by hand exactly as it appears on the transcript, including term, course code, title, subject classification, credits and grade. Errors here are the leading cause of verification delay, because a file with mismatches is returned to you for correction and the clock restarts. A paid service, **Professional Transcript Entry**, will do the entry for you and is worth the fee for anyone with credits from several institutions.
- **Standardized tests**, where required, sent from the testing agency, which takes its own time.

**3. Supporting Information.** Evaluations, meaning letters of recommendation, where you enter each evaluator's name and email and the system requests the letter directly; up to `5` may be entered. Experiences, in the eight categories. Achievements such as awards and honors. Certifications, including EMT, BLS, ACLS and phlebotomy.

**4. Program Materials.** Per-program questions, supplemental essays, program-specific documents, and **prerequisite matching**, where you map your own courses onto each program's required list. This is the step that catches a missing prerequisite, and it is worth doing early rather than in the final week.

**5. Personal Statement.** `5,000` characters including spaces, one essay sent to every program.

**6. Submit and pay.** Roughly `$185` for the first program and about `$65` for each additional one. A **Fee Assistance Program** exists, with a limited number of awards released in batches during the cycle, so it is applied for early.

## Verification, in detail

Verification begins only when three things have all arrived: your submitted application, your payment, and **every** official transcript. One missing transcript holds the entire file, and no one will chase it for you.

CASPA then re-enters and checks your coursework, recalculates cumulative, science and BCP GPAs in its own format, and releases the application to your programs. Typical turnaround is **two to six weeks**, and it stretches at the July through September peak. A file returned for coursework corrections restarts that clock.

## What can and cannot change after submission

| Change | Possible after submitting? |
|---|---|
| Add programs | Yes, and they receive the application as it stands that day |
| Update contact information | Yes |
| Update experience hours | Only in designated update windows, and rules vary |
| Add a new letter writer | Generally yes, before program deadlines |
| Edit coursework or GPA | No, once verified |
| Edit the personal statement | No |

## Reapplying

A new application is submitted each cycle. CASPA offers a reapplication path that carries some information forward, and transcripts must be resent for any institution where you have completed new coursework. Programs frequently ask what changed since the last attempt, so a reapplication with a higher science GPA, more hours, or a new prerequisite is a stronger file than the same one resubmitted.

> **Key:** Rolling admission means the calendar is part of the application. A file verified in June competes for a full class; the same file verified in November competes for whatever seats remain. Working backward from that, the real deadline is roughly two weeks after the portal opens, not the date the program publishes.
keyPoints: Six sections: Personal Information, Academic History, Supporting Information, Program Materials, Personal Statement, and Submit
Coursework must be entered exactly as it appears on each transcript; errors are the leading cause of verification delay and Professional Transcript Entry can do it for a fee
Verification starts only when the submitted application, payment and every official transcript have arrived, then takes roughly two to six weeks
Prerequisite matching inside Program Materials is what catches a missing course, so it is done early
After verification, coursework and the personal statement cannot be edited, though programs can still be added

checks.q: An applicant submits on May 10, pays the same day, and one transcript from a community college attended in 2011 has not arrived. What happens?
choices: Verification proceeds and the missing transcript is requested later
Verification does not begin at all until every official transcript has arrived
The 2011 credits are simply excluded from the GPA calculation
The application is rejected
checks.why: Verification requires the submitted application, payment and every official transcript together. A single outstanding transcript holds the whole file, nobody chases it for the applicant, and the weeks lost land squarely in the rolling review period.

checks.q: Which change is not possible after an application has been verified?
choices: Adding additional programs
Updating a phone number
Editing coursework entries or the personal statement
Adding a letter writer before a program's deadline
checks.why: Coursework and the essay are locked once verified, because the GPAs and the essay have already been distributed. Programs may still be added, contact details updated, and in most cases letters added before individual deadlines.

checks.q: How should an academic or legal background question be handled?
choices: Disclosed honestly with a brief factual explanation
Omitted if the record was expunged or the applicant was a minor
Answered only if a program asks separately
Explained at length in the personal statement instead
checks.why: A disclosed issue with a short factual account is routinely survivable. Nondisclosure discovered later is an integrity finding that ends applications and can end an enrollment after matriculation, which is a far worse outcome than the original issue.

lessons.title: Three timelines, the gap-year math, and where each one breaks
lessons.body:
## Three honest versions of the same plan

The order never changes: certification, the job, the degree and prerequisites while banking hours, then testing, letters, essay and a late-spring submission. What changes is the course load, and it decides everything else.

**Variant A, fast track, roughly `3` years to matriculation.** Twelve credits a semester plus summers, about `30` credits a year. Only realistic with a large block of transferable credit already in hand, and it requires dropping to part-time clinical work, trading patient care hours for calendar time. It also stacks lab sciences, which is where people fail a course.

**Variant B, steady, roughly `4` to `4.5` years.** Nine credits a semester plus one summer course, about `22` credits a year, alongside full-time shifts at `36` hours a week. Sixty remaining credits take about `2.7` years, and hours at matriculation land near `5,000` to `6,000`. This is the default because it is the version that finishes.

**Variant C, part-time school with full-time work, roughly `5` to `6` years.** Six credits a semester, about `15` credits a year. Longest calendar, lowest risk of failing anything, highest hour totals, and the right choice when the transcript needs repair and every remaining grade must be an A.

> **Key:** Every variant produces the same application. The difference is which risk you accept. There is no version where the degree goes faster and the transcript gets stronger at the same time.

## The gap-year math

CASPA opens in late April, programs read on a rolling basis from roughly June, interviews run fall through winter, and classes usually start the next summer. **From submission to the first day of class is roughly `12` to `15` months.**

That interval is only a gap year if you have stopped. Keep working full time through it and those months add roughly `1,700` more patient care hours on top of a finished transcript.

The arithmetic to write down once: a degree finishing in **May of year X** means submitting CASPA in **late April or early May of year X** with spring grades pending, interviewing in **fall of year X**, and matriculating in **summer of year X plus one**. Plan the final prerequisite into that spring semester, because a course still in progress late in the cycle is the commonest reason a complete file is held.

## Where each plan breaks, and the countermeasure

| What kills it | The countermeasure | When to do it |
|---|---|---|
| Submitting late in a rolling cycle | Submit within two weeks of the portal opening; target verification by mid-June | April and May of the application year |
| Coursework entry errors delaying verification | Enter from the official transcript, or pay for Professional Transcript Entry | At data entry |
| One missing prerequisite | Build the program worksheet before registering for the first class; re-verify each spring | Year one, then annually |
| Hours that cannot be verified | Weekly log from payroll records, supervisor contact captured before turnover | Every week |
| A miscategorized experience | Categorize by responsibility, write duties not titles, split mixed roles | At data entry |
| Letters arriving late | Ask in person `6` to `8` weeks out for a **strong** letter; follow up twice | Three months out |
| A missed supplemental application | Track per-program requirements in the worksheet; read email daily | The whole cycle |
| A generic personal statement | Open with one observed moment, answer why PA directly, revise repeatedly | Three to four months out |
| No PA shadowing | Ask a PA on a slow shift for a named number of hours | Years one and two |
| A flat, weak science GPA | Build a long recent run of A grades; target last-60-credit programs | The whole plan |
| Nondisclosure of an academic or legal issue | Disclose honestly and briefly; later discovery is far worse | At data entry |
| Online professionalism problems | Audit public profiles; never post patient details | Now and permanently |

> **Trap:** Nearly every row above is a scheduling or record-keeping problem rather than an ability problem. That is why the plan is built around a worksheet and a log rather than around studying harder.

> **On shift:** The highest-leverage habit here costs ninety seconds a week: open the log, enter the shifts, and once a month check one worksheet row against the program's website.
keyPoints: Fast track needs a large block of existing credit and trades hours for speed; steady at 9 credits a semester takes about 4 to 4.5 years; part-time takes 5 to 6 with the lowest failure risk
From CASPA submission to the first day of class is roughly 12 to 15 months, which is only a gap if you stop working
Plan the final prerequisite into the spring semester of the application year, because a course still in progress late in the cycle holds a file
Submit within about two weeks of the portal opening and target verification by mid-June, since review is rolling
Nearly every application killer is a scheduling or record-keeping failure rather than an ability failure

checks.q: An applicant will finish the degree in May and plans to keep working full time until matriculation. How should the 12 to 15 month interval be described?
choices: A gap year that weakens the application
Wasted time that should be filled with a second degree
Roughly 1,700 additional patient care hours plus a completed transcript, which strengthens the file
A period during which CASPA cannot be submitted
checks.why: The interval between submission and matriculation is structural, not optional, because cycles run a year ahead. Continuing to work converts it into hours and a finished transcript rather than a gap.

checks.q: Why should the last prerequisite be scheduled into the spring semester of the application year rather than the following fall?
choices: Because CASPA will not accept in-progress coursework at all
Because a prerequisite still in progress late in the cycle is a common reason an otherwise complete file is held
Because summer courses are not accepted by most programs
Because fall grades are reported differently
checks.why: Programs review on a rolling basis and many will not extend an interview while a required course is outstanding. A spring completion means the transcript is settled before the file is read, which is the entire advantage of early submission.

checks.q: Which statement about the list of common application killers is most accurate?
choices: Most are caused by insufficient academic ability
Most are resolved by applying to more programs
Most are scheduling and record-keeping failures within the applicant's control
Most are caused by program-specific requirements that cannot be anticipated
checks.why: Late submission, delayed verification, missing prerequisites, unverifiable hours, late letters and missed supplementals are all calendar and documentation problems. That is why the countermeasures are a worksheet, a weekly log, and early requests rather than more study.

cards.front: Why should a program list not be built from rankings?
cards.back: There is no meaningful ranking of PA programs. Build from the ARC-PA and PAEA directories plus each program's required public disclosures: PANCE five-year first-time pass rate, attrition, cost, and program goals.

cards.front: Which four figures is every accredited PA program required to publish?
cards.back: Its accreditation status, its five-year PANCE first-time pass rate, its attrition data, and its cost, along with its program goals. They are posted on the program's own website.

cards.front: Name eight fields the program comparison worksheet must contain.
cards.back: Accreditation status, PANCE pass rate, attrition, total cost, GPA minimums and class average, full prerequisite list with expiration windows, PCE minimum and average, and deadline with rolling status.

cards.front: What are the three filter passes when narrowing a program list?
cards.back: Hard filters that disqualify: prerequisites you cannot finish, hard GPA minimums, a required test you will not take. Soft filters that rank: cost, distance, PCE weighting. Then fit: mission, curriculum, interview format.

cards.front: How many programs should be on a list, and in what proportions?
cards.back: Eight to fifteen, sorted against each program's published class average into programs where you are above it, match it, and fall below it. A list with nothing in the first bucket can produce zero interviews.

cards.front: Which programs should a career changer with strong hours and a weak transcript deliberately include?
cards.back: Programs that weigh patient care experience heavily and programs that calculate a last-60-credit GPA. Applying to fifteen programs that all score the same way means one weakness disqualifies you fifteen times.

cards.front: Which source is authoritative for accreditation status, and why not the program site?
cards.back: ARC-PA, the accrediting commission. Program websites and third-party directories can lag a status change, and status changes are exactly the thing worth catching.

cards.front: When should the program worksheet be re-verified, and why?
cards.back: In the spring of the year you apply. Prerequisite lists, deadlines, test requirements and accreditation status all change annually, and applying against two-year-old data is how a file is rejected for a new requirement.

cards.front: What should you record after calling an admissions office?
cards.back: The name of the person, the date, and the exact answer, entered in the worksheet. A written note of who said what is worth far more months later than a remembered impression.

cards.front: What is cost of attendance, and why does it matter beyond tuition?
cards.back: The school's published budget: tuition and fees, books and equipment, living allowance, transportation and loan fees. It is the ceiling on how much federal aid you may borrow.

cards.front: Give approximate cost of attendance for a public in-state versus a private PA program.
cards.back: Public in-state: about $65,000 tuition and fees plus roughly $50,000 living allowance over 27 months, near $115,000 total. Private: about $125,000 tuition and fees plus the same living costs, near $185,000.

cards.front: What federal aid is available to undergraduates that is not available to graduate students?
cards.back: Pell Grants, which are need-based and never repaid, and Direct Subsidized Loans, where the government pays interest during enrollment. Neither exists at the graduate level.

cards.front: How does graduate federal borrowing work for PA school?
cards.back: Direct Unsubsidized up to an annual limit commonly around $20,500, then Grad PLUS for the remainder up to cost of attendance, with a credit check, a higher rate, and roughly a 4 percent origination fee deducted at disbursement.

cards.front: State the four conditions that must all hold for a PSLF payment to count.
cards.back: The loan is a Direct Loan, you are on a qualifying repayment plan, you are employed full time by a government or 501(c)(3) employer, and the payment is made while all three are simultaneously true.

cards.front: How many PSLF payments are needed, and must they be consecutive?
cards.back: 120 qualifying monthly payments, which need not be consecutive. Submit the employment certification form annually and on every employer change so the count is verified as you go.

cards.front: Why can two PAs doing identical work have opposite PSLF outcomes?
cards.back: Eligibility follows the employer of record, not the job or the location. A hospital employee qualifies; a for-profit staffing company employee working in the same department does not.

cards.front: What does NHSC loan repayment offer, and on what terms?
cards.back: Commonly up to roughly $50,000 for a two-year full-time commitment at an approved shortage-area site, with larger awards at higher-need sites and reduced part-time options. It is applied for once you are working.

cards.front: How does the NHSC scholarship differ from NHSC loan repayment?
cards.back: The scholarship pays tuition, fees and a monthly stipend during school in exchange for two to four years of later service, and is applied for before or during training. Repayment pays down existing debt after you are employed.

cards.front: Name the military routes into PA practice.
cards.back: Health professions scholarship programs through the Army, Navy and Air Force, and the Interservice Physician Assistant Program, which trains serving members with full pay and benefits for a multi-year active duty obligation.

cards.front: What is the decision rule for accepting a service obligation program?
cards.back: Accept only if you would genuinely choose that practice setting anyway. It is a contract, and breaking it triggers repayment of the award plus penalties and interest that exceed what was received.

cards.front: Before registering for any course, what must be verified and with whom?
cards.back: Current offerings and transferability with the institution, and current prerequisite acceptance with each PA program on your list, in writing. All of it changes annually.

cards.front: Which regional community colleges serve as examples for the cheapest prerequisite credit?
cards.back: Camden County College and Rowan College at Burlington County, as examples of the category. In-county tuition commonly runs roughly $150 to $200 per credit, the lowest cost per credit in the whole path.

cards.front: Which regional public four-year institutions serve as examples for degree completion?
cards.back: Rowan University, Rutgers University-Camden, and Stockton University, as examples. In-state tuition commonly runs roughly $400 to $600 per credit, and many now offer evening, weekend and hybrid sections.

cards.front: What do Thomas Edison State University and competency-based online schools offer, and what is the caveat?
cards.back: Adult-focused completion: credit for prior learning, credit by examination, flat-rate self-paced terms at regionally accredited institutions. The caveat is lab science acceptance, which varies by PA program.

cards.front: What is the single question to ask every target program before taking an online lab science?
cards.back: Whether they accept online laboratory courses, asked in writing, with the reply saved. Programs are split, the split widened after 2020, and it has not settled.

cards.front: What are the two separate decisions made about every course you take?
cards.back: Whether the credit transfers toward the degree, decided by the four-year college, and whether the course satisfies a PA prerequisite, decided by each PA program with its own 5 to 7 year expiration window.

cards.front: How does New Jersey's statewide transfer framework generally work?
cards.back: A completed associate degree from a New Jersey community college generally transfers to a New Jersey public four-year with junior standing, with a statewide course-equivalency tool for individual courses. Confirm against the specific major.

cards.front: Give the sequencing rules for prerequisite coursework.
cards.back: Anatomy and Physiology I first, General Chemistry I before organic or biochemistry, statistics and psychology as pairing courses alongside a lab, and never two lab sciences in one semester while working full time.

cards.front: What six things get recorded for every planned or completed course?
cards.back: Institution, course code and title, credits, term, grade, and which PA programs have confirmed they accept it. The last column is re-checked in the spring of the application year.

cards.front: List the fields CASPA requires for each experience entry.
cards.back: Experience type, organization, supervisor name and title with phone and email, start and end dates, hours completed, anticipated hours with a completion date, job title, whether it was paid, and a duty description.

cards.front: Name the eight CASPA experience categories.
cards.back: Patient care, healthcare, volunteer, employment, research, teaching, leadership, and extracurricular activities. You assign the category yourself, and the description is what a reviewer uses to judge whether it is honest.

cards.front: Which hours count and which do not?
cards.back: Hours actually worked count, including overtime and generally orientation and required in-house training. Unpaid meal breaks, cancelled shifts and low-census call-offs do not. Record worked hours, never scheduled hours.

cards.front: What five columns make a defensible hours log?
cards.back: Date, shift start, shift end, hours, and role, with a notes field for anything unusual. Filled weekly from the timekeeping record, it takes about ninety seconds a week.

cards.front: What should you do about supervisor contact information and employer verification?
cards.back: Capture the supervisor's contact details, ideally including a non-work email, before turnover. If they leave, ask human resources who the verifier of record is and whether the employer uses a third-party verification service.

cards.front: What are the two rules for projecting anticipated hours?
cards.back: Do not project past the date you would realistically stop working, and declare the anticipated completion date. Programs expect projections and may ask you to confirm the final total later.

cards.front: How should a role with both patient care and clerical duties be entered?
cards.back: As two entries with an honest hour split and separate descriptions, each matched to its category. Claiming the whole thing as patient care creates a mismatch a reviewer reads as a credibility problem.

cards.front: Write a duty description for an emergency department technician.
cards.back: Obtain 12-lead ECGs, perform venipuncture and point-of-care testing, place and monitor cardiac telemetry, assist with splinting, wound care and reductions, perform CPR in trauma and code response, and trend and report vital signs.

cards.front: What five patterns get an experience entry flagged?
cards.back: A total that does not fit the dates, overlapping employers exceeding plausible hours, an unreachable supervisor, a description contradicting the chosen category, and round numbers everywhere suggesting estimation.

cards.front: Name the six CASPA sections in order.
cards.back: Personal Information, Academic History, Supporting Information, Program Materials, Personal Statement, and Submit. Verification follows submission, payment and the arrival of every official transcript.

cards.front: What are the three parts of Academic History, and which one loses cycles?
cards.back: Colleges Attended, transcripts, and coursework entry, plus standardized tests where required. Coursework entry loses cycles: errors cause the file to be returned for correction, restarting the verification clock.

cards.front: What is Professional Transcript Entry and who should buy it?
cards.back: A paid CASPA service that enters your coursework for you. It is worth the fee for anyone with credits from several institutions, because entry errors are the leading cause of verification delay.

cards.front: What three things must arrive before verification even begins?
cards.back: The submitted application, the payment, and every official transcript. One missing transcript holds the entire file, and no one will chase it on your behalf.

cards.front: What is prerequisite matching, and why do it early?
cards.back: Inside Program Materials you map your own courses onto each program's required prerequisite list. It is the step that catches a missing course, which is a far cheaper discovery in March than in the final week.

cards.front: What can and cannot be changed after verification?
cards.back: You can add programs, update contact information, and usually add a letter writer before deadlines. You cannot edit coursework, recalculated GPAs, or the personal statement.

cards.front: How should background questions about academic or legal history be answered?
cards.back: Honestly and briefly, with a two-sentence factual explanation. A disclosed issue is routinely survivable; the same issue discovered after nondisclosure is an integrity finding that ends applications and enrollments.

cards.front: What does reapplying through CASPA involve?
cards.back: A new application each cycle, with a reapplication path that carries some data forward and transcripts resent wherever new coursework exists. Programs ask what changed, so a stronger GPA, more hours or a new prerequisite matters.

cards.front: Given rolling review, when is the real submission deadline?
cards.back: Roughly two weeks after the portal opens in late April, with verification targeted for completion by mid-June. The published deadline is the last day the door is open, not the day the class is chosen.

cards.front: Describe the three timeline variants and their lengths.
cards.back: Fast track at 12 credits plus summers, about 3 years, requiring existing credit and part-time work. Steady at 9 credits plus a summer course, about 4 to 4.5 years. Part-time at 6 credits, about 5 to 6 years.

cards.front: What does the fast-track variant cost you, and what does the part-time variant cost you?
cards.back: Fast track trades patient care hours for calendar time and stacks lab sciences, which is where courses get failed. Part-time costs only time and carries the lowest risk of failing anything.

cards.front: How long is the interval from CASPA submission to the first day of class?
cards.back: Roughly 12 to 15 months. Submission in late spring, rolling review from June, interviews fall through winter, decisions following, and classes usually starting the next summer.

cards.front: When is the submission-to-matriculation interval actually a gap year?
cards.back: Only if you stop. Continuing to work full time adds roughly 1,700 more patient care hours and a finished transcript, which produces the strongest version of the file you will ever have.

cards.front: Give the year-X arithmetic for a degree finishing in May.
cards.back: Submit CASPA in late April or early May of year X with spring grades pending, interview in fall of year X, and matriculate in summer of year X plus one.

cards.front: Why should the final prerequisite land in the spring rather than the following fall?
cards.back: Programs review on a rolling basis and many will not extend an interview with a required course outstanding. A spring completion settles the transcript before the file is read.

cards.front: Name four application killers and the countermeasure for each.
cards.back: Late submission: submit within two weeks of opening. Entry errors: enter from the transcript or buy Professional Transcript Entry. Missing prerequisite: keep the program worksheet current. Late letters: ask 6 to 8 weeks out in person.

cards.front: What is the common character of nearly every application killer?
cards.back: They are scheduling and record-keeping failures, not ability failures: lost months and missed emails. That is why the plan is built around a worksheet and a weekly log rather than around studying harder.

quiz.q: An applicant builds a program list from a magazine ranking of the top PA schools. What is the principal problem with that approach?
choices: No meaningful ranking of PA programs exists, and the required public disclosures carry the information that matters
Rankings are accurate but only updated every five years
Ranked programs are more expensive on average
Rankings exclude provisionally accredited programs
quiz.why: Accredited programs are required to publish PANCE first-time pass rates, attrition, cost and program goals, which is the real comparative data. A ranking substitutes reputation for outcome data that is already public.

quiz.q: Two programs match on cost and location. Program A publishes a five-year PANCE first-time pass rate of 96 percent with 4 percent attrition. Program B publishes 85 percent with 17 percent attrition. What does that difference most likely reflect?
choices: Program B has a larger class and therefore more variance
Program B admits students it cannot carry, or has an instructional or stability problem
Program B has a more rigorous curriculum
The figures are not comparable between programs
quiz.why: High attrition with a low pass rate is the pairing that matters, because it suggests the program either selects students who cannot succeed there or does not teach them adequately. Both figures are standardized disclosures, so they are directly comparable.

quiz.q: An applicant with 4,500 patient care hours and a 3.05 science GPA builds a list of fifteen programs, all of which state a strong GPA preference and no PCE weighting. What is the flaw?
choices: Fifteen is too many programs for one cycle
The application fees will exceed the fee assistance cap
A single weakness disqualifies the applicant fifteen separate times, with no program scoring the strength
The programs will share information and reject in parallel
quiz.why: Building a list of programs that all score the same way turns one weakness into fifteen rejections. The correction is to deliberately include programs weighting experience heavily and programs using a last-60-credit GPA calculation.

quiz.q: Where should an applicant verify a program's accreditation status?
choices: The program's admissions brochure
The CASPA program directory
A PA student forum
The ARC-PA directory, which is the primary record
quiz.why: ARC-PA grants, continues and withdraws accreditation, so its own listing is the authoritative and most current record. Brochures and third-party directories can lag a status change, which is precisely the event worth catching.

quiz.q: An applicant copied a program's prerequisite list two years ago and plans her final courses from it. What is the risk?
choices: Programs revise prerequisite lists, deadlines and test requirements annually, so the list may be wrong
CASPA will reject coursework entered from an old list
The college will not honor a registration based on outdated information
There is no risk, since prerequisites are set nationally
quiz.why: Prerequisite lists, expiration windows, test requirements and deadlines all change between cycles. Re-verifying every worksheet row in the spring of the application year is the countermeasure, and it takes an afternoon.

quiz.q: A program publishes tuition and fees of $65,000. Why is the applicant's borrowing need likely much higher?
choices: Because tuition rises every semester
Because cost of attendance also includes living expenses, books, transportation and loan fees, which can add $50,000 or more
Because private loans carry mandatory insurance
Because the deposit is not counted in tuition
quiz.why: Cost of attendance is the school's full published budget for a student, and it sets the federal borrowing ceiling. A 27-month program with a $22,000 annual living allowance adds roughly $50,000 to the tuition figure.

quiz.q: A PA student needs $70,000 for one academic year. Direct Unsubsidized covers about $20,500. How is the rest typically borrowed federally?
choices: Direct Subsidized Loans, since graduate students qualify at a higher limit
A Pell Grant supplement
Grad PLUS, with a credit check, a higher rate, and roughly a 4 percent origination fee
Perkins Loans through the institution
quiz.why: Subsidized loans and Pell Grants do not exist at the graduate level, and Perkins is discontinued. Grad PLUS covers the gap up to cost of attendance but costs more, which is why unsubsidized borrowing is exhausted first.

quiz.q: A new graduate takes a job with a for-profit staffing company that places her full time in a nonprofit hospital's emergency department. What is the PSLF consequence?
choices: Her payments qualify, because she works in a nonprofit hospital
Her payments do not qualify, because eligibility follows the employer of record
Her payments qualify at half credit
Eligibility depends on her specialty rather than her employer
quiz.why: PSLF eligibility is determined by who employs her, not by where she works or what she does. This is the reason to ask who signs the paycheck before signing an offer, since ten years of payments can hinge on it.

quiz.q: Which combination is required for a payment to count toward PSLF?
choices: Any federal loan, any repayment plan, and any healthcare employer
A Direct Loan, a qualifying repayment plan, and full-time employment by a government or 501(c)(3) employer, all true at once
Consolidation of all loans plus 60 consecutive payments
Employment in a designated shortage area for 5 years
quiz.why: All three conditions must hold simultaneously for each of the 120 payments, which need not be consecutive. FFEL and Perkins loans qualify only after consolidation into a Direct Consolidation Loan, and shortage-area service describes NHSC, not PSLF.

quiz.q: A student is offered an NHSC scholarship covering tuition, fees and a stipend in exchange for later service. What is the central consideration?
choices: Whether the stipend is taxable
Whether the scholarship reduces Grad PLUS eligibility
Whether it can be combined with PSLF
Whether she would choose that practice setting anyway, since breach triggers repayment plus penalties and interest
quiz.why: A service obligation is a contract, and the financial penalty for breaking it substantially exceeds the value received. The decision rule is to take it only when the required practice setting is one you would have chosen without the money.

quiz.q: A graduate carries $150,000 in federal debt with a starting salary near $110,000. How should this ratio be characterized?
choices: Roughly one year of gross income, which is heavy but manageable, and driven mainly by program tuition
Unmanageable and a reason to abandon the pathway
Irrelevant, since PSLF discharges all balances automatically
Better than finishing a bachelor's degree and stopping, in every case
quiz.why: A debt-to-income ratio near one is demanding but workable, and the single largest lever on it is which program you attend. PSLF requires ten years of qualifying payments with a qualifying employer, so it is a plan, not an automatic outcome.

quiz.q: An applicant plans to complete Anatomy and Physiology I and II online at a regionally accredited university. What must be verified first?
choices: That the courses carry at least 4 credits each
That each PA program on her list accepts online laboratory courses, confirmed in writing
That the university is nationally rather than regionally accredited
That the lab kit ships to New Jersey
quiz.why: PA programs are split on online lab sciences and the split has not settled since 2020. Because the answer varies by program and can change, it is asked of each target program directly and the reply is saved.

quiz.q: An applicant took Anatomy and Physiology I in 2015 and earned a B. It transfers for degree credit at her four-year school. What should she expect from PA programs?
choices: Universal acceptance, since the credit transferred and the grade was adequate
Acceptance only at programs that require a B or better
That many programs cap science prerequisites at 5 to 7 years, so it may have to be retaken
That CASPA will exclude it from the science GPA
quiz.why: Degree credit and prerequisite acceptance are independent decisions by different institutions. A course can count toward graduation indefinitely while falling outside a PA program's prerequisite recency window, and CASPA still counts the old grade in the GPA.

quiz.q: Which sequencing plan is most appropriate for someone working 36 hours a week?
choices: Anatomy and Physiology II with General Chemistry II in the same semester
Anatomy and Physiology I paired with statistics
Microbiology with Organic Chemistry I in the same semester
Three lab sciences over one summer term
quiz.why: One lab science paired with a non-lab course is the sustainable combination, and A and P I comes first because it anchors the sequence. Two lab sciences at once while working full time is where people fail a course, which costs the retake and the GPA permanently.

quiz.q: What does New Jersey's statewide transfer framework generally provide?
choices: That a completed New Jersey community college associate degree transfers to a New Jersey public four-year with junior standing
That all community college courses satisfy PA program prerequisites
That out-of-state credits transfer automatically
That science prerequisites never expire within the state
quiz.why: The framework addresses degree transfer between New Jersey public institutions, with a course-equivalency tool for individual courses. It says nothing about PA program prerequisite acceptance or expiration, which are separate decisions by each program.

quiz.q: Why are Camden County College, Rowan University and Thomas Edison State named in the planning lesson?
choices: Because they have articulation agreements with PA programs
Because their credits are guaranteed to satisfy PA prerequisites
As examples of three categories of institution, with the standing instruction that offerings and acceptance change and must be verified
Because they are the only regionally accredited options in the area
quiz.why: They illustrate community college, public four-year, and adult-focused completion routes. Nothing about a named institution is a recommendation or a guarantee, because catalogs, transferability and program acceptance all change annually.

quiz.q: An applicant reconstructs three years of shifts from memory in April of the application year and enters 5,200 hours. What is the risk?
choices: CASPA will cap the entry at 5,000 hours
The total may not reconcile with the dates and schedule, and it cannot be defended if questioned
Hours over 5,000 are not counted by programs
Reconstructed hours must be entered as volunteer experience
quiz.why: Programs divide hours by the date range and compare against a plausible schedule. About 1,728 hours a year is full time, so a number that does not reconcile invites a question the applicant cannot answer from memory.

quiz.q: Which of these should be excluded when logging patient care hours?
choices: Overtime shifts
Required in-house technician training
Cancelled and low-census shifts that were scheduled but not worked
Hours worked on holidays
quiz.why: The standard is hours actually worked. Overtime and required training generally count; scheduled shifts that were cancelled did not happen. Recording scheduled rather than worked hours is the most common source of an indefensible total.

quiz.q: An applicant's former supervisor left the hospital and cannot be reached. What is the best remedy?
choices: Remove the experience entry rather than risk an unverifiable claim
Ask human resources who the verifier of record is and whether a third-party verification service is used
List a coworker as the supervisor
List the hospital's main phone number with no name
quiz.why: Employers maintain employment records independent of any individual manager, and many use a verification service. Deleting real hours forfeits the strongest part of the file, and listing a coworker or a bare phone number as the supervisor misrepresents the entry.

quiz.q: An applicant will keep working for eight months after submitting. How should those hours be handled?
choices: Entered as anticipated hours with a stated completion date
Omitted entirely, since only completed hours count
Added to the completed total to keep the entry simple
Entered as a separate volunteer experience
quiz.why: Projected hours are expected and explicitly supported, since applicants are usually still working. They must be declared as anticipated with a completion date rather than folded into the completed figure, and programs may ask for confirmation later.

quiz.q: Which experience description is most useful in a CASPA entry?
choices: Emergency department technician, full time, nights
Worked hard in a fast-paced environment as part of a great team
Assisted nurses and physicians with various tasks as needed
Obtain 12-lead ECGs, perform venipuncture and point-of-care testing, place and monitor cardiac telemetry, assist with splinting and wound care, participate in trauma and code response
quiz.why: Reviewers read the duty description to judge whether the category claimed is honest and whether the experience carried real responsibility. Titles, schedules and adjectives convey nothing about what the applicant actually did.

quiz.q: An applicant submits and pays on May 5, but a transcript from a single summer course taken in 2012 has not arrived. What happens to the timeline?
choices: Verification proceeds and the transcript is added on arrival
Verification does not start at all, and the delay lands inside the rolling review period
CASPA excludes the 2012 course from the GPA and continues
The application is returned unprocessed
quiz.why: Verification requires the submitted application, payment and every official transcript together. A single missing document holds the file, and since programs review on a rolling basis, weeks lost in June are seats lost.

quiz.q: Which CASPA step most often causes a file to be returned to the applicant and the verification clock to restart?
choices: Entering evaluators in Supporting Information
Errors in hand-entered coursework
Completing program-specific supplemental essays
Selecting the wrong experience category
quiz.why: Every course must be entered exactly as it appears on the transcript, and mismatches cause the file to be returned for correction. Professional Transcript Entry exists as a paid service specifically because this step costs applicants weeks.

quiz.q: Which action is no longer possible once an application has been verified?
choices: Adding a program to the list
Updating a mailing address
Editing coursework entries and the personal statement
Adding a letter writer before a program's deadline
quiz.why: GPAs are recalculated from the coursework and the essay is distributed at verification, so both are locked. Programs may still be added, receiving the application as it stands, and contact details and letters generally remain editable.

quiz.q: An applicant was placed on academic probation in 2013 and wonders whether to disclose it on the background questions. What is correct?
choices: Disclose it honestly with a brief factual explanation
Omit it, since it is more than ten years old
Omit it and explain only if a program asks at interview
Disclose it only if the institution reports it on the transcript
quiz.why: A disclosed issue with a short factual account is routinely survivable. Nondisclosure later discovered is an integrity finding, which ends applications and can end an enrollment after matriculation, an outcome far worse than the original event.

quiz.q: Inside Program Materials, what does prerequisite matching accomplish?
choices: It calculates the applicant's science GPA for each program
It requests transcripts from the colleges attended
It maps the applicant's courses onto each program's required list, which is what surfaces a missing course
It confirms the program's accreditation status
quiz.why: Prerequisite matching is the step where a course that is absent from the record becomes visible against a specific program's requirements. Doing it early leaves time to register for the course; doing it in the final week does not.

quiz.q: A program publishes a November 1 deadline. Given rolling review, when is the practical deadline?
choices: November 1, since that is the published date
October 1, allowing one month for verification
Within roughly two weeks of the portal opening in late April, with verification complete by mid-June
September 1, the midpoint of the cycle
quiz.why: Rolling programs fill interview slots continuously, so a file verified in June competes for a full class while the same file verified in the autumn competes for remainders. The published deadline is the last day the door is open, not the day the class is chosen.

quiz.q: An applicant with 60 credits remaining wants to matriculate as quickly as possible and asks about the fast-track variant. What is the honest trade?
choices: Twelve credits a semester requires cutting to part-time clinical work, trading patient care hours for calendar time and stacking lab sciences
Twelve credits a semester is no harder than nine and simply finishes sooner
Fast-tracking increases patient care hours because the schedule is more efficient
Fast-tracking is generally preferred by admissions committees
quiz.why: A 30-credit year alongside full-time shifts is not realistic, so the hours slow while the credits accelerate. It also forces lab sciences to be paired, which is the specific circumstance in which applicants fail a prerequisite.

quiz.q: An applicant finishing her degree in May worries about a gap year before matriculation. What is the accurate framing?
choices: It is a real gap and she should enroll in a master's program to fill it
The 12 to 15 month interval is structural, and continuing to work converts it into roughly 1,700 more hours and a finished transcript
She should delay CASPA by a year to avoid the gap
Programs view any interval between graduation and matriculation unfavorably
quiz.why: Cycles run about a year ahead, so the interval exists for everyone. Continuing to work through it strengthens the file rather than creating a gap, and delaying submission would simply push matriculation another full year.

quiz.q: Why should the last prerequisite be scheduled for the spring semester of the application year rather than the following fall?
choices: Because CASPA does not accept in-progress coursework
Because spring grades are weighted more heavily
Because many programs will not extend an interview with a required course still outstanding late in a rolling cycle
Because summer and fall courses are not transferable
quiz.why: Rolling review means interviews are offered as files are read, and an outstanding prerequisite gives a program a reason to hold the file. Finishing in spring settles the transcript before review, which is the entire point of submitting early.

quiz.q: Reviewing the common application killers, what do nearly all of them have in common?
choices: They reflect insufficient academic ability
They are program-specific and cannot be anticipated
They are resolved by applying to more programs
They are scheduling and record-keeping failures within the applicant's control
quiz.why: Late submission, delayed verification, a missing prerequisite, unverifiable hours, late letters and missed supplementals are all calendar and documentation failures. That is why the countermeasures are a worksheet, a weekly log and early requests.

quiz.q: Which pairing of killer and countermeasure is correct?
choices: Letters arriving late; ask in person 6 to 8 weeks ahead for a strong letter and follow up at two and four weeks
Missing a prerequisite; add more programs to the list
Unverifiable hours; increase the total to compensate
A generic personal statement; submit it earlier in the cycle
quiz.why: Letters are the one component another person controls, which is why they are requested earliest with explicit follow-up. Adding programs does not supply a missing course, inflating hours makes verification worse, and an early generic essay is still generic.

scenarios.title: Building the list from twenty programs to nine
scenarios.intro: You are eighteen months from applying. Your file will be roughly a 3.2 cumulative GPA, a 3.1 science GPA with a strong upward trend over the last 40 credits, about 4,800 emergency department technician hours by submission, one prerequisite still outstanding, and no standardized test taken. You have twenty programs in a spreadsheet and need to get to a real list.

steps.prompt: The twenty rows are half empty. Some have tuition, a few have GPA minimums, none have attrition or PANCE data. Where do you start?

choices.text: Fill in accreditation status from ARC-PA and the required disclosures from each program site: PANCE five-year first-time rate, attrition, cost, and program goals
choices.feedback: Correct. These are published because programs are required to publish them, and they are the only standardized comparative data that exists. Accreditation comes from ARC-PA rather than the program's own page, because status changes there first.

choices.text: Sort the twenty by a published ranking and cut the bottom half
choices.feedback: There is no meaningful ranking of PA programs. Sorting by one substitutes reputation for the outcome data that programs are obligated to disclose.

choices.text: Email all twenty admissions offices asking what they look for in an applicant
choices.feedback: You will get twenty polite generic replies. Save the contact for a specific question the website does not answer, and record the name and date when you do.
